notes: Every table has one row per county keyed by fips (VARCHAR, 5 digits). Join tables with USING (fips).
Missing, suppressed and not-applicable values are NULL. There are no -9999 / -8888 sentinels left.

Store, restaurant and recreation-facility COUNTS (groc*, superc*, convs*, specs*, ffr*, fsr*, recfac*) are NULL when suppressed (fewer than 3 in 2020, zero in 2016). NULL is not zero; the data cannot identify counties with exactly zero stores.
Columns flagged is_state_level are the same for every county in a state: they cannot rank counties within a state.
Atlas column names end in a 2-digit data year; PCH_/CH_ columns are changes between two years.
State totals live in health_rankings_state, never in the county tables.

glossary.term: limited access to healthy food / low food access / food desert share
glossary.definition: Share of a county's population that is BOTH low-income AND lives far from a supermarket (more than 1 mile urban / 10 miles rural). This is the County Health Rankings 'Limited Access to Healthy Foods' definition.

not.food_access.pct_laccess_pop19: all residents far from a store regardless of income; much larger and mostly measures rurality

glossary.definition: Share of residents (or of eligible residents) receiving SNAP. The Atlas only publishes this at STATE level, so it cannot rank counties within a state.
use: food_assistance.pc_snapben22 (SNAP benefits per capita, dollars, county-level proxy)
food_access.pct_laccess_snap19 (SNAP households far from a store, county-level)

not.food_assistance.pct_snap22: STATE-level: identical for every county in a state

glossary.definition: Share of adults with BMI >= 30. The Atlas value is STATE-level (same for every county). No county-level obesity exists in this database; the live CDC PLACES tool (fetch_cdc_places, measure OBESITY) is the county-level source.

Share of adults with diagnosed diabetes. Two county-level versions exist: Atlas 2019 (crude, CDC Diabetes Surveillance) and Rankings 2020 (age-adjusted, BRFSS). Say which one you used; do not average them.

not.food_health.pct_diabetes_adults15: older year; use only when the user asks about 2015 or change over time

glossary.definition: Share of people lacking adequate access to food. The Atlas measure is STATE-level (3-year CPS average); the Rankings measure (Map the Meal Gap 2020) is county-level.
Share of residents below the federal poverty line, 2021 SAIPE.
Metro status is a county classification (OMB 2023); % rural is a population share (Census 2010). Prefer metro23 for grouping counties, pct_rural for a continuous measure.
Share of adults under 65 (or children under 19) without health insurance, SAHIE 2020.
Grocery stores per 1,000 residents (2020). Low density is a different concept from 'limited access', which is distance-based and income-conditioned.

glossary.term: counties with no supermarket / zero stores / store deserts
glossary.definition: Store and restaurant counts come from County Business Patterns, which suppresses small counts: 2020 columns are NULL when a county has fewer than 3 establishments, 2016 columns when it has none. The database therefore cannot say that a county has ZERO grocery stores or supercenters; it can say the count is suppressed (fewer than 3). Count NULLs as 'suppressed', never as 0.
use: food_stores.groc20 IS NULL  (fewer than 3 grocery stores)
food_stores.grocpth20 (stores per 1,000 residents, also NULL when suppressed)

not.COALESCE(food_stores.superc20, 0) = 0: turns 'suppressed' into 'zero' and overstates store deserts

glossary.term: child food insecurity / food insecurity among children
glossary.definition: NO county-level child food insecurity measure exists in this database. The Atlas food insecurity columns are STATE-level and cover households, not children. Report that the child measure is unavailable, then use the all-ages county measure, labelled as all ages.
use: health_rankings.pct_food_insecure (all ages, county-level; label it 'all ages, not children')
health_rankings.pct_enrolled_in_free_or_reduced_lunch (students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, county-level)

not.food_insecurity.foodinsec_21_23: STATE-level household measure, not a child measure

glossary.definition: Atlas columns end in a 2-digit year (e.g. _19 = 2019, _22 = 2022). When a variable has two years, the larger suffix is the latest. PCH_/CH_ columns are the change between the two years, not a level.
